Return to the illustrated tour · Tour source

These are the behavior changes made alongside the restructuring. Most ordinary analyses retain their results. The cases below deliberately behave differently because the previous behavior was broken or unsafe. Each item explains what could go wrong and points to the code and a test that protects the fix.

The production implementation was qualified at commit 0a9f9d8. Subsequent comment and test improvements preserve its numerical implementation. The later worker-error repair improves failure reporting and rejects missing results; normal scientific results remain checked by the manual comparison. The detailed review record is the behavior ledger; its older planning sections are historical, while final acceptance records completion. “Regression test” below means a test designed to prevent the same bug returning.

Importing counts and preserving inputs

1. Unsorted count-file entries could lose or misplace counts

Example / old behavior. A file can list cells in the order 2, 1, 2. The import code assumed entries for each cell were already together. It could build an incorrect sparse matrix; some entries could be missing even when a basic matrix-validity check passed.

Fix. Sort private working copies by cell and feature before constructing the matrix. Carry values with their coordinates and keep explicit zero entries.

Code / test. create_csc_matrix() in import_functs.R; test-refactor-import-coordinates.R checks every expected coordinate, value and matrix pointer, including an example that previously lost entries. Review: B1/L08.

2. Interleaved Cell Ranger feature types could get the wrong row numbers

Example / old behavior. Feature rows can be ordered gene, guide, gene, guide, gene. The importer treated each type as a contiguous block and subtracted its minimum feature ID to get local row numbers. That mapping is wrong for interleaved types.

Fix. Match the actual feature IDs into the gene and guide row lists. Preserve the supplied gene, guide and cell names/order.

Code / test. Cell Ranger import in import_functs.R; test-refactor-import-coordinates.R uses five alternating feature rows and independently specified gene/guide matrices. Review: B1/L08.

3. Repeated file coordinates needed an explicit rejection rule

Example / old behavior. A file might contain two entries for the same cell and feature. Keeping both as separate entries could produce an invalid compressed sparse matrix. Adding them together would choose a new interpretation of the input counts.

Fix and decision. Eugene explicitly chose a clear import error for repeated (cell, feature) coordinates. The Cell Ranger and Parse constructors reject them before native matrix operations. This concerns file coordinates; it does not reject repeated guide-metadata rows or redefine existing R triplet inputs. The external ondisc file parser is a separate implementation.

Code / test. import_functs.R and test-refactor-import-coordinates.R. See decision D2026-10-16-01.

4. Symmetric dense matrices could lose their lower-triangle values

Example / old behavior. Importing the dense matrix rbind(c(1, 2), c(2, 3)) could lose a lower-triangle entry. Matrix could first choose a compact symmetric representation, while SCEPTRE subsequently treated its stored entries as a general matrix. A nearly symmetric input could also lose its distinct supplied value.

Fix. Convert to a general matrix representation before making it sparse. Preserve all supplied entries and names. This can require an additional copy for dense inputs; sparse/backed inputs are not made dense.

Code / test. set_matrix_accessibility() in storage.R; test-refactor-storage-dense.R checks both triangles, near-symmetry, public import and resulting cell totals. Review: B7.

5. Sorting sparse coordinates could modify the caller’s matrix

Example / old behavior. Converting a triplet matrix to row- or column-based storage could sort arrays that were still shared with the input. Code retaining an alias to the input could then see its coordinates or values change.

Fix. Make sure the working arrays belong to the conversion before sorting them. Reuse arrays already created privately by a constructor, and copy borrowed ones when needed. Preserve stored values, order within equal coordinates and special floating-point values.

Code / test. storage.R; test-refactor-storage-ownership.R checks the input and aliases before/after both conversion directions, including negative zero and a specified NaN bit pattern. Review: T8/CL2.

6. Computing mitochondrial summaries could alter the supplied gene indices

Example / old behavior. The C++ summary code converted mitochondrial gene indices from R numbering to C++ numbering by decrementing the supplied vector. A subsequent use of the same R vector could then refer to different genes.

Fix. Convert a private copy and leave the supplied vector unchanged.

Code / test. sparse_matrix_functs.cpp and storage.R; test-refactor-storage-ownership.R checks repeated calls, unchanged inputs and mitochondrial fractions computed directly from the matrix. Review: native I2/T8.

7. Reading guide assignments could alter saved memberships

Example / old behavior. The assignment getter used an in-place native index-decrement operation on what should have been temporary data. With a single guide, the flattened vector could still share storage with the saved membership vector.

Fix. Build a new zero-based index vector using ordinary R subtraction. The getter’s existing output classes and single-guide behavior are preserved.

Code / test. get_grna_assignments() in getters_and_setters.R; test-refactor-assignment-getter.R checks repeated full/QC-filtered reads and unchanged saved memberships. Review: L18/T8.

8. Constructing trans pairs could change the caller’s positive-control table

Example / old behavior. Passing a data.frame of positive-control pairs to trans-pair construction could turn that caller’s object into a data.table. The conversion was performed by reference while processing exclusions.

Fix. Make a local copy before performing the data.table operations. Returned pair values, ordering and exclusion rules stay the same.

Code / test. construct_trans_pairs() in pair_constructor_functs.R; test-refactor-pair-construction.R checks both input classes, all exclusion modes and unchanged caller objects. Review: L06/O1.

Selecting pairs, cells and model fits

9. Unsorted gene positions could omit valid cis pairs

Example / old behavior. At midpoint 100 and distance 20, positions 90, 1000, 110 should select the first and third genes. The old scan stopped after leaving the first in-range block, so it missed the third.

Fix. Check the inclusive distance condition for every supplied position. Return qualifying rows in their original order.

Code / test. compute_genes_within_distance() in pair_construction_functs.cpp; test-refactor-pair-construction.R checks this exact example, endpoints and the public cis-pair constructor. This repair can change the affected requested pair family. Review: B2.

10. Genomic midpoint and distance arithmetic could overflow

Example / old behavior. Two individually valid genomic endpoints near 1.8 billion can have a sum too large for a signed 32-bit integer. Computing their midpoint or subtracting distant coordinates in that type could produce an incorrect result.

Fix. Use a wider numeric type before addition/subtraction, and check that coordinates passed to native code are representable. Keep the existing inclusive distance definition and row order.

Code / test. pair_constructor_functs.R, pair_construction_functs.cpp and test-refactor-pair-construction.R cover a wide midpoint and distances spanning the ordinary integer range. Unsafe old examples were not executed. Review: B2/T2.

11. An accepted intercept-only formula could fail with NT controls

Example / old behavior. formula_object = ~ 1 is accepted. Selecting rows of its one-column design matrix could turn it into a vector because R drops single dimensions by default. Later matrix calculations could then fail with “non-conformable arguments.”

Fix. Keep the design two-dimensional with drop = FALSE when selecting common and guide-specific fit cells.

Code / test. analysis_context.R and association_workers.R; test-refactor-context-execution.R independently calculates the intercept score for NT calibration/discovery with both permutation and CRT. Review: B3.

12. An old response fit could be reused after its fitting inputs changed

Example / old behavior. After calibration using NT controls, a user could switch to complement controls while retaining the same formula. The old reset check compared formula syntax, so a fit for the previous cells could remain. The same formula can also produce a different design matrix when factor contrasts change.

Fix. Clear incompatible saved response fits when the actual design or control choice changes. Keep the existing assignment/cell-change rules explicit, and keep guide-specific NT-discovery fits separate from reusable calibration fits.

Code / test. fit_cache.R and analysis_context.R; test-refactor-cache.R checks changed controls, changed factor contrasts and discovery–calibration– discovery sequences against runs with saved fits cleared.

Calibration and unsafe requests

13. Overlapping NT groups could request more sampled cells than exist

Example / old behavior. Two NT groups of eight cells can overlap inside a ten-cell dataset. Adding their sizes gives 16, even though their union has at most ten cells. Using 16 as a without-replacement sample size could make the native sampler index outside its storage.

Fix. Bound the required permutation sample size by the valid analysis-cell universe and preserve the union-based treatment selection for this case.

Code / test. preprocessing_functions.R and generate_samples_functions.cpp; test-refactor-calibration-safety.R checks overlapping groups and a complete public high-MOI calibration run. The unsafe old native call was not executed. Review: S1.

14. Calibration group-size checks could use guides that no longer had cells

Example / old behavior. Metadata can still list an NT guide after QC has removed all its assigned cells. A calibration request based on that metadata can then ask for more active groups than exist.

Fix. Validate the requested group size against NT groups that actually remain after QC. Reject an impossible request with a clear error; do not silently choose a smaller group size or a different statistical analysis.

Code / test. check_functions.R and preprocessing_functions.R; test-refactor-calibration-safety.R removes one or more groups through public QC while leaving metadata intact, then checks explicit and default group-size requests. Review: S1/S2.

15. Invalid or oversized native requests could reach unsafe arithmetic or indexing

Example / old behavior. Cases included a sample larger than its universe, an invalid CRT probability, a resampling-budget sum above integer capacity, a calibration candidate-count product that overflowed, or a reached skew-normal stage with fewer than 100 draws. Some could reach unchecked native operations.

Fix. Check the relevant sizes, ranges and products before allocation, integer conversion or indexing. Check only stages/prefixes actually used. Keep valid empty draws, probability endpoints and variable CRT sample sizes. This does not introduce a blanket tightening of all public argument validation.

Code / test. sampling_safety.h, generate_samples_functions.cpp, negative_control_functions.cpp, low_level_full_test.cpp and check_functions.R and preprocessing_functions.R; test-refactor-calibration-safety.R covers small safe reproductions, overflow rejection and valid edge cases. Review: S1/S2.

16. One mixture-assignment bound checked the wrong parameter

Example / old behavior. The check for the upper perturbation-start value in g_pert_guess_range accidentally read pi_guess_range. A valid mixing- proportion range could therefore let an invalid perturbation range through.

Fix. Compare the perturbation bound with the perturbation parameter. The documented upper value 20 is accepted; 20.1 is rejected.

Code / test. check_assign_grna_inputs() in check_functions.R; test-refactor-legacy-boundaries.R checks below, at and above the bound, while ordinary EM and fallback behavior have separate retained tests. Review: B5/L11.

Files, temporary memory and error handling

The following fixes concern cleanup when an operation fails. R errors can leave C++ functions without running their usual cleanup code. The tests deliberately trigger small controlled errors; they do not exhaust the machine’s memory.

17. Failed reads or writes could leave file connections open

Example / old behavior. The Matrix Market metadata reader and pipeline vector writer closed their connections after success. An error during reading or writing could bypass that close.

Fix. Register cleanup immediately after opening each helper’s connection, so it also runs when the helper exits with an error.

Code / test. get_mtx_metadata() in import_functs.R and write_vector() in ondisc_functs.R; test-refactor-file-lifetimes.R checks plain/gzip success and injected read/write failures, including that only the helper’s own connection is closed. Review: B5/L09/T7.

18. A failure while creating a draw pointer could leave the sampled bank allocated

Example / old behavior. A C++ collection of sampled cell indices could already exist when R allocated or registered the pointer used to return it. An R error at that point could bypass cleanup of the collection.

Fix. Prepare the protected R pointer before creating the native bank, then transfer the bank safely into it. Keep the existing sampler streams and draws.

Code / test. generate_samples_functions.cpp and sampling_safety.h; tools/checks/test-sampling-ownership.R checks three controlled failure points for each of three production samplers (nine cases).

19. Count routines could leave temporary C++ buffers allocated on an R error

Example / old behavior. Converting an R input or constructing an R return value while C++ count buffers were still alive could bypass their cleanup.

Fix. Prepare R inputs/outputs before creating the count buffers, perform the native calculation, and finish using the buffers before returning to operations that can raise an R error. Supplied coordinate vectors stay unchanged.

Code / test. sparse_counts.cpp and sparse_matrix_functs.cpp; tools/checks/test-count-ownership.R checks 214 controlled cases and an intentionally unsafe comparison that proves the checker can detect the problem.

20. Returning calibration or association results had a similar cleanup gap

Example / old behavior. Temporary calibration-group/pair containers or selected null statistics could still occupy C++ buffers when R allocated the final result. An R error in that conversion could leave those buffers allocated.

Fix. Arrange cleanup around the exact result being converted, so it runs on success and on an R error. Allocate only the reached result/selected null segment; avoid an eager buffer for unused resampling stages.

Code / test. result_lifetime.h, negative_control_functions.cpp and inference_stages.cpp; tools/checks/test-result-ownership.R checks 959 controlled cases across 12 workloads plus an unsafe comparison. These probes cover the declared buffers and error points, not every possible Rcpp allocation. Review: B8.

21. Dispersion fitting could hide unrelated allocation or system failures

Example / old behavior. A catch-all C++ handler treated every exception from dispersion fitting like a numerical fitting problem. An allocation or system failure could therefore look like an ordinary numerical fallback.

Fix. Preserve the established handling of numerical domain/overflow errors, but let unrelated allocation, system and other failures propagate. The estimator, iteration order, clipping and numerical fallback values are preserved.

Code / test. compute_nb_size_param_functions.cpp; tools/checks/test-dispersion-exceptions.R checks 14 current-estimator error-policy cases. The separate manual historical probe retains 107 numerical comparisons and 14 paired failure cases. Review: B5.

Plotting

22. QC plotting ignored supplied appearance/downsampling options

Example / old behavior. A caller could request a different point size, transparency or number of downsampled pairs through plot_run_qc(), but the pairwise plot was called without those values.

Fix. Forward the documented arguments to the pairwise plot.

Code / test. plotting_functions.R; test-refactor-legacy-boundaries.R checks actual layer size/transparency and sampled pair identities, plus the unchanged default and single-plot return cases. Review: B4/L13.

23. High guide-count thresholds could break histogram construction

Example / old behavior. Counts 0, 1, 11, 15 with an explicit threshold 16 or 40 could trigger expansion intended for counts beyond the single-bin range. The resulting request could have a negative number of expansion bins.

Fix. Expand only when counts exceed the actual single-bin limit, rather than using the unrelated fixed value 10 as the trigger.

Code / test. plotting_functions.R; test-refactor-legacy-boundaries.R checks those exact thresholds, bin labels, default behavior and unchanged RNG state. Review: B4/L15.

24. Volcano colors could disagree with the stored significance calls

Example / old behavior. Recreating plot colors from a strict p-value cutoff could omit the largest significant p-value or handle ties differently from the result table. A significant result at the drawn cutoff could be colored as nonsignificant.

Fix. Use the existing significant column for the colors. Leave scientific calls and p-values unchanged.

Code / test. make_volcano_plot() in plotting_functions.R; test-refactor-legacy-boundaries.R checks cutoff ties with explicitly different stored flags. Review: B4/L14.

25. A QQ confidence band could disappear from some facets

Example / old behavior. The band code chose one group across the whole plot. If panel A contained groups 1/2 and panel B groups 3/4, that choice could leave panel B without a band.

Fix. Select one group independently inside each panel. Keep the existing order-statistic band formula.

Code / test. qq_plot_helpers.R; test-refactor-legacy-boundaries.R checks both panels against the beta-quantile calculation and retains single- panel behavior. Review: B4/L20.

26. Asking for extra diagnostics could make valid discovery results vanish from plots

Example / old behavior. output_amount = 2 or 3 adds diagnostic columns. A valid early-stage or empirical-tail result can have missing skew-normal parameters, and saved null distributions can contain padding. Whole-table na.omit() could then discard valid results, even showing zero discoveries where the ordinary output showed a significant result.

Fix. Require completeness only in the fields the plots need: p-value, log fold-change and significance flag. Optional diagnostic missingness no longer removes the result; missing essential plotting fields still do.

Code / test. Discovery plotting in plotting_functions.R; test-refactor-plot-diagnostic-na.R compares built QQ/volcano/text data across output amounts 1/2/3 for both data.frame and data.table results. Review: B9.

A memory improvement, distinct from the bugs above

Guide-vector aggregation no longer makes the entire sparse input dense

The old in-memory collapse_grna_matrix() first converted the complete guide matrix to a dense matrix. A large sparse assay could therefore require a large avoidable allocation just to sum guides belonging to the same vector.

The replacement prepares sparse row access and sums selected groups in column blocks. The returned vector-by-cell matrix remains dense. First-seen vector order, cell order, repeated-metadata multiplicity and this platform’s dense column-sum rounding are preserved. One complete selected column is the minimum block; there is no universal peak-memory bound.

Code / test. import_functs.R; test-refactor-vector-aggregation.R uses explicit sums, duplicate/rounding examples and block-edge cases. Old/new implementation equality remains in the manual suite. New backed vector aggregation is still future work. Review: B6/T11.

Costs and work that remains

The refactor is not uniformly cheaper in memory. Two costs were accepted explicitly: eight-million-entry numeric-triplet conversions added about 122–123 MiB peak RSS in their measured cases, and a final Papalexi cold serial workflow rose from about 505 to 667 MiB. The cause of the latter increase remains unresolved. Final acceptance gives the exact measured commits, resource scopes and limits. The dense-conversion correctness fix also has its separately measured extra-copy cost.

Several issues were deliberately left for later decisions: Bonferroni guide/ target interpretation in plots, a global rather than per-bin downsampling cap, broader malformed-input validation, and a new dispersion fallback policy. Backed CRT, backed vector aggregation, SPA, Wilcoxon and accelerated fitters remain extensions to implement and validate separately.

There was no general redefinition of stored zero/fractional counts, scientific significance or the pairwise QC rule. The old/new comparison covers its agreed ordinary cases; the regression tests above specify the intended corrections.

Worker errors

27. A parallel worker failure could hide its original error

Example / old behavior. A worker could report “Cannot read response gene_X”, while the parent subsequently failed with “$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors” when combining its outputs. A child exiting without replying could also leave an incomplete block unrecognized.

Fix. Check each returned block before reporting success or combining results. Report the failed worker’s block number and original error. Distinguish a missing reply from a successful empty result, so empty work blocks remain valid. Successful result order and random seeds are unchanged.

Code / test. execution.R and test-worker-errors.R cover serial and forked errors, a child exiting before replying, valid empty results, empty internal CRT dispatch, successful order and preserved cause text.
